title: Learning Rate & Schedules
hook: The single most important hyperparameter: set it too high and training diverges, too low and it crawls — so we warm it up, then decay it.
key_points: The learning rate scales how big a step gradient descent takes each update.
Too high overshoots or diverges; too low wastes compute and stalls.
Warmup ramps the rate up early to avoid unstable first steps.
Decay schedules (cosine, step, linear) shrink it later to settle into a minimum.
content_html: The learning rate controls how far the parameters move along the gradient at each training step. It is consistently the hyperparameter that matters most: get it wrong and even a perfect model and dataset won't train. Rather than picking one fixed value, modern training varies it over time with a schedule.
extra_html:
How it works

Set the rate too high and updates overshoot the minimum, causing the loss to bounce or blow up; set it too low and training inches along, burning compute. A common recipe is a short warmup — starting tiny and ramping up over the first few hundred steps to avoid wild early updates — followed by a decay phase that gradually shrinks the rate so the model can settle. Cosine, step, and linear decays are popular shapes. Adaptive optimizers like Adam adjust an effective per-parameter rate on top of this global schedule.

Why it matters

Almost every training failure or success traces back to the learning rate. Warmup-then-decay schedules became standard for training large transformers because they keep the early phase stable and the late phase precise. Understanding the rate demystifies a lot of training folklore: it's why batch size, warmup length, and decay shape are tuned so carefully in practice.

related.title: Gradient Descent
related.hook: Lost in fog on a hillside, you'd feel for the steepest downhill step and take it, again and again. That's how models learn.

related.title: Adam: The Default Optimizer
related.hook: Adam gives every parameter its own adaptive step size by tracking the gradient's recent average and spread — and it mostly just works.

related.title: AdamW: Decoupled Weight Decay
related.hook: L2 regularization and weight decay are the same thing for plain SGD - but not for Adam. Decoupling them fixes Adam's generalization and makes the best decay value independent of the learning rate.
